raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

FIX #63358

A Hermes response can contain a valid `<tool_call>` and then a later region that is not a call. Non-streaming parsing dropped every call, and streaming never sent the text after the bad region. Each region is now parsed on its own: valid calls are kept, and the first region that cannot be a call, plus the text after it, is content.

This is not a duplicate of #63327. That PR restores streaming text after a stray tag in prose (#63309) and does not change non-streaming `extract_tool_calls`. A valid call followed by a bad region still loses the call on current main. This change covers that case and also keeps the stray-tag prose path consistent.

AI assistance was used to prepare this patch. The parser change is limited to Hermes (Longcat inherits it) plus an opt-in flush at stream end.

## Claims

- A valid tool call before a malformed `<tool_call>` region is returned, on both streaming and non-streaming paths.
- The malformed region and the text after it are returned as content. Streaming and non-streaming agree, including an empty unclosed tag flushed when generation ends.
- A lone bad region still returns the original text and no tool calls.
- A well-formed tool call is unchanged: only the prefix before the first call is content, and text after a successful call is still omitted.
- A literal `<tool_call>` in prose is content, not a dropped suffix and not a tool call, even if the prose contains `"name"`.

## Validation

Parser-only bug. No model weights or generation are involved, so there is no model evaluation.

`ruff` 0.14.0 `check` and `format --check` passed on:

- `vllm/tool_parsers/hermes_tool_parser.py`
- `vllm/parser/abstract_parser.py`
- `tests/tool_parsers/test_hermes_tool_parser.py`

This machine cannot `import vllm` from the checkout (`transformers` requires `huggingface-hub<1.0`, and 1.15.0 is installed), so pytest was not run here. The new cases were executed by loading `hermes_tool_parser.py` from `HEAD` and from this branch.

Input:

```text
First. <tool_call>
{"name": "get_weather", "arguments": {"city": "Paris"}}
</tool_call> Second. <tool_call>not json</tool_call> Third.
```

`HEAD`:

- non-streaming: `tools_called=False`, content is the entire raw string (the weather call is dropped)
- streaming: content is `First. `, tool name `get_weather`, and ` Second. <tool_call>not json</tool_call> Third.` is never sent

This branch:

- both paths: one `get_weather` call with `{"city": "Paris"}`
- both paths: content is `First.  Second. <tool_call>not json</tool_call> Third.`

Stray prose `The literal <tool_call> tag opens a call. Done.`:

- `HEAD` streaming content is `The literal `
- this branch, both paths: the full sentence and no tool call

The same loader checked chunk sizes 1, 3, and 8 for the issue's other trailing regions (`<tool_call>`, `<tool_call> opens a call. Done.`, `<tool_call></tool_call> Third.`), a normal tool call, two sequential calls, and plain text. Streaming matched non-streaming.

CI selects `tests/tool_parsers` from `.buildkite/test_areas/misc.yaml` when `vllm/tool_parsers/` changes.

## Details

`extract_tool_calls` ran `json.loads` on every regex match inside one `try`. Any bad region raised and the fallback returned the raw string with no calls.

`extract_tool_calls_streaming` walked regions in order and `break`ed when a region had no tool name, so later text was left unsent. `_extract_content` also stops at the first `<tool_call>` and never resumes.

The patch splits regions by the start and end tags. A region is a call only when its body is a JSON object with `name` and `arguments`. The first failure ends tool parsing. If at least one call succeeded, content is the prefix before the first call plus everything after the last good call. If none succeeded, the raw string is returned, which preserves the old fallback for a single bad region and for incomplete JSON such as a missing closing brace.

Streaming uses the same split. A body that does not start with `{`, or a closed body that is not a call, is emitted as content and later tags are not parsed. An empty unclosed tag stays buffered, because a JSON payload may still arrive, but the prose before that tag is sent. `finish_streaming` emits the held tag when generation ends. Hermes sets `flush_streaming_on_finish` so the serving flush calls it without turning Hermes into an engine-based parser. That flag would change `_engine_based` for the whole delegating parser and is not required here.

An incomplete `{...` region that has already streamed a function name is not retracted if the final JSON is invalid. The streaming API cannot take a tool call back, and that incomplete-name case already streamed a call on main.

## Checklist

- [x] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. (Mandatory for agents, optional for humans).
- [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR.
- [x] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity.
- [x] **Testing and Validation:** Validates the change and ensures any added tests are meaningful and reliable, with CI coverage or documented CI resource constraints and validation performed outside CI.
- [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Keeps code and comments clear and concise, and updates relevant documentation and examples.
- [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Includes a brief summary and relevant links, supports claims with evidence, explains root causes and implementation trade-offs, and follows the contributing guide.

Hi @YLlllllllllll, thanks for picking this up! Just a heads-up: when I filed #63358 I had already linked a fix on my fork (https://github.com/its-amann/vllm/commit/25be7ef1659e8919f8245ff58de1ff0997bfcd1f) and asked for feedback on the approach before opening a PR. The two approaches look pretty similar. Happy to go with whatever the maintainers prefer, or to collaborate here so we don't end up with duplicate PRs.

Thanks for flagging the fork commit. This PR is the non-streaming half of #63358 as well: one bad region no longer drops earlier valid calls. #63327 restores streaming text after a stray tag and leaves `extract_tool_calls` unchanged, so the two are not the same patch. Happy for maintainers to keep one of them.

The follow-up commit buffers the text before an unresolved `<tool_call>` until that region is known to be a call or not, which is what the review comment asked for.

## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.

If a chunk ends at the second `<tool_call>` tag, the text between the calls is sent before we know whether that call is valid. Non-streaming drops that text when both calls are valid. Could we buffer it until the second call is resolved?

files.patch:
@@ -420,3 +420,235 @@ def test_hermes_streaming_content_and_tool_call_in_single_chunk(
     assert tool_parts[0].function.name == "f"
     args_str = "".join(tc.function.arguments or "" for tc in tool_parts)
     assert json.loads(args_str) == {"x": 1}
+
+
+_WEATHER_CALL = (
+    '<tool_call>\n{"name": "get_weather", "arguments": {"city": "Paris"}}\n</tool_call>'
+)
+
+
+class _DummyTokenizer:
+    """Tokenizer stand-in. These cases feed text directly to the parser."""
+
+
+def _hermes_request() -> ChatCompletionRequest:
+    return ChatCompletionRequest(model="test-model", messages=[])
+
+
+def _stream_hermes(text: str, chunk_size: int) -> tuple[str, list[dict[str, str]]]:
+    parser = Hermes2ProToolParser(_DummyTokenizer())
+    request = _hermes_request()
+    previous = ""
+    content_parts: list[str] = []
+    tools: dict[int, dict[str, str]] = {}
+    for offset in range(0, len(text), chunk_size):
+        delta_text = text[offset : offset + chunk_size]
+        current = previous + delta_text
+        delta = parser.extract_tool_calls_streaming(
+            previous_text=previous,
+            current_text=current,
+            delta_text=delta_text,
+            previous_token_ids=[],
+            current_token_ids=[],
+            delta_token_ids=[],
+            request=request,
+        )
+        previous = current
+        if delta is None:
+            continue
+        if delta.content:
+            content_parts.append(delta.content)
+        for tool_call in delta.tool_calls or []:
+            slot = tools.setdefault(tool_call.index, {"name": "", "arguments": ""})
+            function = get_function_delta(tool_call)
+            if function.name:
+                slot["name"] += function.name
+            if function.arguments:
+                slot["arguments"] += function.arguments
+    flushed = parser.finish_streaming()
+    if flushed is not None and flushed.content:
+        content_parts.append(flushed.content)
+    ordered = [tools[index] for index in sorted(tools)]
+    return "".join(content_parts), ordered
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "trailing",
+    [
+        " Second. <tool_call>",
+        " Second. <tool_call> opens a call. Done.",
+        " Second. <tool_call></tool_call> Third.",
+        " Second. <tool_call>not json</tool_call> Third.",
+    ],
+)
+def test_hermes_keeps_calls_before_malformed_region(trailing: str) -> None:
+    """A later malformed region must not drop earlier valid tool calls.
+
+    Regression for https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/63358.
+    """
+    text = f"First. {_WEATHER_CALL}{trailing}"
+    result = Hermes2ProToolParser(_DummyTokenizer()).extract_tool_calls(
+        text, _hermes_request()
+    )
+
+    assert result.tools_called
+    assert len(result.tool_calls) == 1
+    assert result.tool_calls[0].function.name == "get_weather"
+    assert json.loads(result.tool_calls[0].function.arguments) == {"city": "Paris"}
+    assert result.content == f"First. {trailing}"
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "text",
+    [
+        "The literal <tool_call> tag opens a call. Done.",
+        'Mention <tool_call> and "name": "foo" in prose.',
+        "Use <tool_call> when you want a tool.",
+    ],
+)
+def test_hermes_stray_tool_call_in_prose_stays_content(text: str) -> None:
+    """A literal tag in prose is content on both paths.
+
+    Regression for https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/63309.
+    """
+    result = Hermes2ProToolParser(_DummyTokenizer()).extract_tool_calls(
+        text, _hermes_request()
+    )
+    content, tools = _stream_hermes(text, chunk_size=1)
+
+    assert not result.tools_called
+    assert result.content == text
+    assert content == text
+    assert tools == []
+
+
+def test_hermes_lone_malformed_region_returns_raw_text() -> None:
+    text = "<tool_call>not json</tool_call> Third."
+    result = Hermes2ProToolParser(_DummyTokenizer()).extract_tool_calls(
+        text, _hermes_request()
+    )
+
+    assert not result.tools_called
+    assert result.tool_calls == []
+    assert result.content == text
+
+
+def test_hermes_well_formed_output_is_unchanged() -> None:
+    text = f"Hello {_WEATHER_CALL} thanks"
+    result = Hermes2ProToolParser(_DummyTokenizer()).extract_tool_calls(
+        text, _hermes_request()
+    )
+
+    assert result.tools_called
+    assert result.tool_calls[0].function.name == "get_weather"
+    # Text after a successful call stays dropped, matching the previous parser.
+    assert result.content == "Hello "
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("chunk_size", [1, 3, 8])
+def test_hermes_streaming_matches_nonstreaming_on_trailing_malformed(
+    chunk_size: int,
+) -> None:
+    text = f"First. {_WEATHER_CALL} Second. <tool_call>not json</tool_call> Third."
+    nonstreaming = Hermes2ProToolParser(_DummyTokenizer()).extract_tool_calls(
+        text, _hermes_request()
+    )
+    content, tools = _stream_hermes(text, chunk_size)
+
+    assert content == nonstreaming.content
+    assert len(tools) == 1
+    assert tools[0]["name"] == "get_weather"
+    assert json.loads(tools[0]["arguments"]) == {"city": "Paris"}
+
+
+def test_hermes_streaming_buffers_empty_unclosed_tag_until_finish() -> None:
+    text = f"First. {_WEATHER_CALL} Second. <tool_call>"
+    parser = Hermes2ProToolParser(_DummyTokenizer())
+    request = _hermes_request()
+    delta = parser.extract_tool_calls_streaming(
+        previous_text="",
+        current_text=text,
+        delta_text=text,
+        previous_token_ids=[],
+        current_token_ids=[],
+        delta_token_ids=[],
+        request=request,
+    )
+    assert delta is not None
+    assert delta.content == "First. "
+    assert delta.tool_calls
+    assert get_function_delta(delta.tool_calls[0]).name == "get_weather"
+
+    flushed = parser.finish_streaming()
+    assert flushed is not None
+    assert flushed.content == " Second. <tool_call>"
+
+
+def test_hermes_streaming_holds_text_between_calls_until_second_resolves() -> None:
+    """Text between calls stays buffered until the next region is resolved.
+
+    A chunk that ends on the next ``<tool_call>`` must not emit that text.
+    A valid follow-up call drops it, matching non-streaming. A malformed
+    follow-up emits it.
+    """
+    request = _hermes_request()
+    opened = f"First. {_WEATHER_CALL} between <tool_call>"
+
+    valid_parser = Hermes2ProToolParser(_DummyTokenizer())
+    opened_delta = valid_parser.extract_tool_calls_streaming(
+        previous_text="",
+        current_text=opened,
+        delta_text=opened,
+        previous_token_ids=[],
+        current_token_ids=[],
+        delta_token_ids=[],
+        request=request,
+    )
+    assert opened_delta is not None
+    assert opened_delta.content == "First. "
+
+    valid_tail = '{"name": "get_time", "arguments": {"tz": "UTC"}}</tool_call>'
+    valid_text = opened + valid_tail
+    valid_delta = valid_parser.extract_tool_calls_streaming(
+        previous_text=opened,
+        current_text=valid_text,
+        delta_text=valid_tail,
+        previous_token_ids=[],
+        current_token_ids=[],
+        delta_token_ids=[],
+        request=request,
+    )
+    assert valid_delta is not None
+    assert valid_delta.content is None
+    names = [
+        get_function_delta(tool_call).name
+        for tool_call in valid_delta.tool_calls or []
+        if get_function_delta(tool_call).name
+    ]
+    assert names == ["get_time"]
+    assert valid_parser.finish_streaming() is None
+
+    bad_parser = Hermes2ProToolParser(_DummyTokenizer())
+    bad_parser.extract_tool_calls_streaming(
+        previous_text="",
+        current_text=opened,
+        delta_text=opened,
+        previous_token_ids=[],
+        current_token_ids=[],
+        delta_token_ids=[],
+        request=request,
+    )
+    bad_tail = "not json</tool_call> tail"
+    bad_text = opened + bad_tail
+    bad_delta = bad_parser.extract_tool_calls_streaming(
+        previous_text=opened,
+        current_text=bad_text,
+        delta_text=bad_tail,
+        previous_token_ids=[],
+        current_token_ids=[],
+        delta_token_ids=[],
+        request=request,

inline_comments.body:
Buffered now. A chunk that ends on the next `<tool_call>` no longer emits the text since the previous call. That text stays held until the region is resolved:

- a valid call drops it, matching non-streaming
- a region that cannot be a call emits it, together with the rest of the output
- if generation ends while the tag is still open, `finish_streaming` emits the held text and the tag

Covered by `test_hermes_streaming_holds_text_between_calls_until_second_resolves`.

Hi @YLlllllllllll, thanks for picking this up! Just a heads-up: when I filed #63358 I had already linked a fix on my fork (https://github.com/its-amann/vllm/commit/25be7ef1659e8919f8245ff58de1ff0997bfcd1f) and asked for feedback on the approach before opening a PR. The two approaches look pretty similar. Happy to go with whatever the maintainers prefer, or to collaborate here so we don't end up with duplicate PRs.

Thanks for flagging the fork commit. This PR is the non-streaming half of #63358 as well: one bad region no longer drops earlier valid calls. #63327 restores streaming text after a stray tag and leaves `extract_tool_calls` unchanged, so the two are not the same patch. Happy for maintainers to keep one of them.

The follow-up commit buffers the text before an unresolved `<tool_call>` until that region is known to be a call or not, which is what the review comment asked for.
